answer.rationale: Primary region p99 latency at 5x target with heavy settlement writes at peak. Rollback is blocked by compliance-mandated security patch. Regional failover (memory_b2) has proven fast latency recovery and clean traffic shift in similar degradation scenarios. Read replica routing (memory_b5) addresses non-write load but doesn't solve the write path bottleneck that's driving current p99. Capacity additions take time we don't have during settlement peak. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) contain failures but don't resolve underlying latency. Failover to secondary region isolates the primary's write path issue, maintains transactional integrity, and allows settlement traffic to complete under known-good infrastructure while we investigate the new release's impact in the degraded primary. This preserves the security patch while protecting availability.
